title: Termination Conditions

basis.scope: Canonical bounded termination conditions for REDUCE_025 outputs after deterministic selection is defined, including termination measure semantics, strict progress, and termination classes without asserting universal termination.

core_rule.statement: Termination is bounded by a well-founded reduction measure and strict progress across lawful reductions; failure is terminal; NF(C), pNF(C), and classified ⊥C_x are terminal outcomes; RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Define the bounded conditions under which REDUCE_025 is guaranteed to terminate. This patch establishes termination classes without asserting universal termination.

canonical_claims.statement: Termination is bounded by a well-founded reduction measure and strict lawful progress.
The reduction measure μ(C) is evaluated after EVAL_024.
Bounded termination does not imply universal termination.

formal_objects.name: Termination
formal_objects.definition: A property indicating that REDUCE_025 reaches a reduction outcome after a finite number of lawful reduction steps.

formal_objects.name: Reduction Measure
formal_objects.definition: A well-founded measure used to evaluate reduction progress.

formal_objects.name: Reduction Progress
formal_objects.definition: Each lawful reduction strictly decreases the reduction measure.

formal_objects.name: Termination Class
formal_objects.definition: Classification of continuation expressions according to bounded termination behavior.

termination_classes.description: Termination proven for the bounded continuation subclass.
Infinite lawful reduction cannot presently be excluded.

progress_rules: Reduction measure is evaluated after EVAL_024.
Every lawful reduction must strictly decrease μ(C).
Equivalent traces do not alter μ(C).
invariants: NF(C), pNF(C), and ⊥C_x are terminal outcomes.

next_recommended_patch.title: Canonical Form Uniqueness Conditions
next_recommended_patch.purpose: Define the bounded conditions under which the canonical normal form of a continuation is unique modulo process equivalence. This patch establishes uniqueness semantics without asserting a universal uniqueness proof.
